## Evidence-backed memo: DeadReckon’s purpose, need, and unique value

### Executive finding

DeadReckon began as an omnibus response to 25 unmet needs around agentic coding, but its coherent product thesis is narrower:

> Make coding-agent work predictable enough to delegate by turning an agent session into a durable, isolated, independently verified lifecycle object.

The originating research says the opportunity is “operational infrastructure for safe delegation,” not merely history capture or local versioning ([REPORT.md](/Users/gdc/stoa/docs/research/2026-05-10-unmet-needs/REPORT.md:5), especially lines 7–9). The current product statement is consistent: supervise existing agents, record file-backed state/evidence, gate completion, then promote accepted work into an artifact ([PRODUCT.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/PRODUCT.md:14), lines 16–21). The README sharpens it further: the agent codes; DeadReckon decides when “done” is real and returns evidence rather than a transcript ([README.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/README.md:5), lines 5–10; [CONCEPTS.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/CONCEPTS.md:7), lines 9–15).

That trust boundary—not “support every agent workflow”—is the load-bearing identity.

### Originating unmet needs

The original research’s top cluster was explicitly about making agentic coding “predictable enough to delegate”: live context/spend, multi-agent coordination, undo, provenance, memory, cross-tool state, observability, sandboxes, and billing controls ([REPORT.md](/Users/gdc/stoa/docs/research/2026-05-10-unmet-needs/REPORT.md:5), lines 7–9).

The top 10 were:

1. Live context and spend ([REPORT.md](/Users/gdc/stoa/docs/research/2026-05-10-unmet-needs/REPORT.md:17), lines 17–29).
2. Multi-agent worktree coordination: task claiming, shared context, branch isolation, merge sequencing ([REPORT.md](/Users/gdc/stoa/docs/research/2026-05-10-unmet-needs/REPORT.md:40), lines 40–52).
3. Per-turn undo/rewind ([REPORT.md](/Users/gdc/stoa/docs/research/2026-05-10-unmet-needs/REPORT.md:64), lines 64–76).
4. Prompt-to-code provenance ([REPORT.md](/Users/gdc/stoa/docs/research/2026-05-10-unmet-needs/REPORT.md:87), lines 87–99).
5. Searchable team memory ([REPORT.md](/Users/gdc/stoa/docs/research/2026-05-10-unmet-needs/REPORT.md:111), lines 111–123).
6. Cross-tool state sharing ([REPORT.md](/Users/gdc/stoa/docs/research/2026-05-10-unmet-needs/REPORT.md:135), lines 135–147).
7. Serious operator UI ([REPORT.md](/Users/gdc/stoa/docs/research/2026-05-10-unmet-needs/REPORT.md:158), lines 158–170).
8. Traces, evals, and failure RCA ([REPORT.md](/Users/gdc/stoa/docs/research/2026-05-10-unmet-needs/REPORT.md:182), lines 182–194).
9. Disposable sandboxes ([REPORT.md](/Users/gdc/stoa/docs/research/2026-05-10-unmet-needs/REPORT.md:206), lines 206–218).
10. Billing guardrails ([REPORT.md](/Users/gdc/stoa/docs/research/2026-05-10-unmet-needs/REPORT.md:230), lines 230–242).

Honourable mentions added permissions, MCP tooling, onboarding, structural verification, discoverable gates, provider routing, handoff, port/env isolation, governance receipts, local-first data, team standards, efficiency evals, and a run queue; the audit preserves the complete vocabulary ([AUDIT-2026-05-11.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AUDIT-2026-05-11.md:9), lines 11–37).

### The abstractions DeadReckon is actually built around

These are the strongest reusable patterns, in descending order of importance.

1. **Intelligence is replaceable; the boundary is the product.** DeadReckon wraps existing CLI/API agents rather than competing with them ([CONCEPTS.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/CONCEPTS.md:26), lines 28–41). This makes provider choice an implementation detail while preserving workflow, state, and verification.

2. **Judgment and invariants live in different layers.** Markdown skills own agent-facing judgment; Rust owns state, locks, sandboxing, providers, and gates ([AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:229), lines 231–243). This is the core “harness of harnesses” abstraction.

3. **A run is a durable lifecycle object, not a terminal session.** State is persisted before meaningful changes, with PID-aware locks, append-only ledgers, crash recovery, resume, kill, undo, and promotion ([AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:101), lines 101–107; glossary at lines 1725–1739). This directly abstracts “walk away, return later, still know reality.”

4. **Work and acceptance are separated.** The provider can propose `Done`; only the gate can transition toward promotion. A failed gate feeds corrective evidence back into another turn rather than ending the run ([AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:1135), lines 1137–1144).

5. **“Done” is compiled into executable behavior.** Project detection, operator criteria, deterministic linting, goal/contract reconciliation, and a bounded critic make acceptance a pre-spend artifact rather than a retrospective claim ([AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:3392), lines 3394–3424).

6. **Verification produces promotion, not merely success text.** Accepted work atomically becomes a library artifact; `Completed` is intended to imply durable promotion ([AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:1587), lines 1593–1605).

7. **Evidence is projected, never invented.** Spend, traces, provenance, events, flight records, snapshots, proofs, and docs are durable sources; TUI, reports, narrative, and verdicts are projections over them. `RunView` is the explicit one-read-model expression of this pattern ([AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:3441), lines 3443–3455). PRODUCT formalizes “evidence before elegance” ([PRODUCT.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/PRODUCT.md:36), lines 38–47).

8. **One verified run is the compositional atom.** Chains sequence ordinary runs ([AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:1995), lines 1997–2005); plans spawn normal run subprocesses and merge their artifacts ([AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:2102), lines 2104–2112); campaigns lift fork→merge one level without inventing another executor ([AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:2381), lines 2383–2400).

9. **Extension is allowed around the trust root, not through it.** Policy, catalog, hooks, and event sinks are swappable JSON-over-stdio workers, but the gate is deliberately non-swappable ([AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:2784), lines 2786–2800; [SEAMS.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/SEAMS.md:1), lines 3–5).

10. **Persisted facts are becoming a protocol.** The new protocol crate is intentionally pure wire vocabulary with no I/O, async runtime, or dependency on other DeadReckon crates ([deadreckon-protocol/src/lib.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-protocol/src/lib.rs:4), lines 4–20). That is a natural extension of the evidence-first design.

### What is genuinely unique

The strongest unique combination is:

- existing subscription/API agent as the intelligence;
- isolated, recoverable run lifecycle;
- operator-authored/compiled done contract;
- separate verification process;
- tamper-aware proof;
- signed promotion;
- post-hoc re-verification (`VERIFIED`, `REGRESSED`, `UNVERIFIED`);
- the same gate applied to run, plan, chain, and campaign outputs.

The July needs update explicitly says competitors have moved on subagents, checkpoints, costs, and durable goals, while DeadReckon’s signed tamper-evident gate remains the differentiator ([UNMET-NEEDS-OPTIONS-2026-07-01.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/UNMET-NEEDS-OPTIONS-2026-07-01.md:34), lines 36–39). It also identifies “fork with a gate” as the uniquely DeadReckon form of multi-agent orchestration (lines 80–90).

The most defensible positioning is therefore:

> Agent CLIs provide intelligence. DeadReckon provides the provider-neutral control plane and evidence boundary that makes their work safely delegable.

### Evolution and contradictions to preserve in the map

1. **The purpose narrowed while the feature surface widened.**  
   V0 mapped almost one-for-one onto the top-10 needs. Current positioning leads with watchdog trust and auditable output. That narrowing is healthy. But the implementation later accumulated Course, Helm, Contract, Logbook, narration, campaign, seams, learning/self-improvement, distribution, descriptor contracts, and steering. Any functionality map should judge each addition by whether it strengthens the trustworthy-delegation loop, not merely whether it is impressive.

2. **The central “secret the agent cannot read” claim is stronger than the implementation currently proves.**  
   README says the watchdog holds a secret the agent process cannot read ([README.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/README.md:59), lines 61–63), and AS-BUILT repeats that only `dr-gate` reads the nonce ([AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:1076), lines 1078–1087). In source, however:

   - the nonce is a normal file under the run root ([state.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/state.rs:195), lines 201–209);
   - the marker uses Rust `DefaultHasher`, not a cryptographic MAC ([gate.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/gate.rs:751), lines 751–791);
   - macOS Seatbelt starts with `(allow default)` and provider launches pass no gate read denylist ([commands.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-sandbox/src/commands.rs:149), lines 173–209; [cli_common.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-providers/src/cli_common.rs:55), lines 79–95);
   - `none` is explicitly an available backend ([commands.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-sandbox/src/commands.rs:18), lines 26–37).

   The project itself admits HMAC-grade signing remains backlog ([UNMET-NEEDS-OPTIONS-2026-07-01.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/UNMET-NEEDS-OPTIONS-2026-07-01.md:165), lines 165–167). So the gate is presently best described as a strong process/protocol invariant plus tamper evidence, not yet a cryptographic trust boundary against a hostile local agent. This is the most important half-baked item because it sits under the product’s core claim.

3. **“Resolved” sometimes means “an alpha slice exists,” not “the user need is met.”**

   - Searchable library artifacts caused Need #5 to be marked resolved ([AUDIT-2026-05-11.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AUDIT-2026-05-11.md:15), lines 17–18), but the later options memo identifies run-memory carryover as one of the loudest still-unmet pains ([UNMET-NEEDS-OPTIONS-2026-07-01.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/UNMET-NEEDS-OPTIONS-2026-07-01.md:104), lines 106–120). Search is not memory injection.
   - Read-only import caused cross-tool state to be marked resolved, but exportable handoff remains unbuilt. Import is not shared state or bidirectional continuity.
   - Generated docs caused team onboarding to be marked resolved, but this proves artifact availability, not that teams successfully onboard from it.

   The map should distinguish “primitive implemented” from “need outcome achieved.”

4. **`fork` has two incompatible meanings in the docs.**  
   Plan execution already has `fork <plan-id>` and launches ready tasks ([AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:2147), lines 2149–2152). Yet the same architecture says user-facing sub-agent forking is not built (lines 1707–1710), meaning ad hoc `fork <run-id> --prompt`. The July memo also calls that missing. The vocabulary must distinguish “start planned children” from “branch a live/finished run into a child.”

5. **Provider support is broader than provider evidence parity.**  
   README visually presents six supported CLIs ([README.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/README.md:43), lines 43–52), but Pennant explicitly says Gemini and OpenCode still have evidence-backed contract gaps ([CHANGELOG.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/CHANGELOG.md:34), lines 36–41 and 59–65). Execution support should not be presented as equal-quality spend, resume, answer extraction, and flight observability.

6. **Maturity documentation is stale and internally inconsistent.**  
   README says production-release track and implemented/tested lifecycle ([README.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/README.md:54), lines 54–57). Cargo is `0.6.0` ([Cargo.toml](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/Cargo.toml:12), lines 12–18), while AS-BUILT still claims workspace `0.1.0` pending tagging and says its last update was May 31 ([AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:3), lines 3–8; line 117). The architecture has later sections appended, but its header/version claims are not reliable maturity evidence.

### Purpose-level preservation/deprecation signal

| Family | Need strength | Purpose-level judgment |
|---|---|---|
| Done contract → independent gate → proof → promotion → verdict | Direct, central, unique | Essential. Preserve first; harden nonce isolation and cryptographic signing before extending. |
| Durable run state, locks, resume, kill, undo, worktree isolation | Direct, high-frequency origin need | Essential control-plane substrate. |
| Spend, trace, provenance, snapshots, flight, `RunView` | Direct origin need and required to substantiate trust | Essential, but consolidate ledgers/read models rather than add more projections. |
| Provider-neutral CLI/API boundary and descriptor contracts | Direct provider-routing/cross-tool need | Essential. Preserve the contract-as-data approach; label parity gaps honestly. |
| Plan/fork/merge and chains | Direct coordination need | Essential direction. Decide a canonical decomposition model and vocabulary; overlapping run/plan/chain/campaign concepts risk user and maintenance complexity. |
| Library/import/docs/handoff | Direct memory/state/handoff needs | Valuable but still half-achieved as a user outcome. Preserve primitives; build carryover/handoff before calling the need resolved. |
| Attach/Helm/Logbook | Direct observability/UI need | Preserve shared read models, five-question spine, cited evidence, and responsiveness. Visual effects are non-essential. |
| Campaign meta-orchestration | Coordination-adjacent | Decision needed. It is sophisticated, but queueing and port/env brokerage—the original operational gaps—remain missing. This may be premature breadth. |
| Course automatic shape planner | Indirect support for coordination and cost safety | Useful UX layer, not identity. Keep only if real usage proves it chooses better than explicit/simple launch paths. |
| Live/orchestrated narrator | Indirect observability/handoff | Preserve deterministic evidence projection; scrutinize multiple model-backed narrator paths and skills for duplication/cost. |
| Composable seams | Architecture-driven rather than strongly origin-research-driven | Potential platform value, weak proven user need. Keep the fixed trust-root rule; require adoption evidence before broadening. |
| Local self-improvement loop | No clear originating unmet need | Strongest cruft/deprecation candidate at purpose level. It is an interesting dogfooding experiment, but it expands into proposal/eval/PR automation outside the core delegation contract. |
| Motion/effects/theme machinery | No originating need; PRODUCT says decoration is optional | Cruft candidate. Must never compete with evidence, latency, or clarity. |
| Release/update/signing machinery | Product delivery requirement, not unique user functionality | Maintain as infrastructure; exclude from the conceptual product map except as distribution/release integrity. |

### Recommended north-star test

For every feature, ask:

1. Does this make an unattended run safer to delegate?
2. Does it make state or evidence more durable, truthful, or recoverable?
3. Does it preserve provider independence?
4. Does it strengthen independent verification or safe promotion?
5. Does it reduce operator reconstruction from transcripts?
6. Can it compose from the verified-run primitive without inventing another parallel model?

If the answer is no to most of these, the feature is outside DeadReckon’s essential identity even if technically mature.
